questions.q: A body starting from rest moves along a straight line with a constant acceleration. The variation of speed (v) with distance $(s)$ is represented by the graph
questions.solution:
For a body moving with constant acceleration $a, v=u+a t$ Since the body starts from rest, $u=0$
\therefore \quad v=a t which is a straight line passing through the origin. Hence the correct graph is (2).

questions.q: A body is projected horizontally with a velocity of $4 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm\sec$. The velocity of the body after 0.7 seconds will be nearly (Take $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm\sec^2$ )
questions.solution:
After $0.7 \mathrm\sec$ the horizontal velocity component of the body $=4 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm\sec$ since there is no change in velocity in horizontal direction.
The vertical velocity component after 0.7 seconds $=0+g t=0+0.7 \times 10=7 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm\sec\therefore$ Resultant velocity of the body $=\sqrt{(4 \sqrt{2})^2+7^2}=\sqrt{32+49}=9 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm\sec$

questions.q: The displacement $x$ of a particle varies with time $t$ as $x=a e^{-a t}+B^{\beta x}$, where $a, b, \alpha$ and $\beta$ are positive constants. The velocity of the particle will:
questions.solution: From question $\begin{aligned} & x=a e^{-\alpha \mathrm{t}}+b e^{\beta t} \\ & V=\frac{d x}{d t}=-a \alpha e^{-x t}+b \beta_e^{\mathrm{B}+} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}=-a \alpha e^{-t}+b \beta \varepsilon^{\beta t} \end{aligned}\therefore$ We can tell that velocity will increase with time since the negative component will decrease with an increase in time and the positive component will increase in the equation given equation.

questions.q: Two bodies $\mathrm{A}$ (of mass $1 \mathrm{~kg}$ ) and $\mathrm{B}$ (of mass $3 \mathrm{~kg}$ ) are dropped from heights of $16 \mathrm{~m}$ and $25 \mathrm{~m}$, respectively. The ratio of the time taken by them to reach the ground is:
questions.solution: We know that time taken by a body from height $h$ to reach the ground is. $\begin{aligned} t & =\sqrt{\frac{2 h}{g}} \\ \therefore \quad \frac{t_{\mathrm{A}}}{t_{\mathrm{B}}} & =\frac{\frac{2 h_{\mathrm{A}}}{g}}{\frac{2 h_{\mathrm{B}}}{g}}=\sqrt{\frac{h_{\mathrm{A}}}{h_{\mathrm{B}}}} \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{16}{25}}=\frac{4}{5} . \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A bullet emerges from a barrel of length $1 . 2m$ with a speed of $640ms^{- 1}$. Assuming constant acceleration, the approximate time that is spent in the barrel after the gun is fired is
questions.solution:
Given, $s = 1.2m, v = 640\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}, a = ? , u = 0; t = ?$

We have the third equation of motion

$2as = v^{2} - u^{2}$

$2a \times 1.2 = 640 \times 640$

Or $a = \dfrac{8 \times 64 \times {10}^{3}}{3}$

And by first equation of motion

$v = u + at$

Or $t = \dfrac{v}{a} = \dfrac{15}{4} \times {10}^{- 3}$

$= 3.75 \times {10}^{- 3}s \approx 4ms$

Let \(u\) be the initial velocity.
\(\therefore v_{1}=u+a t_{1}, v_{2}=u+d  \left($t_{3}+t_{2}\right)$\mathrm{and}$\)
\(v_{3}=u+a\left($t_{1}+t_{3}+t_{3}\right)\)
Now, \(v_{1}=$\frac{u w_{1}}{2}, \frac{u\left(u+a t_{1}\right)}{2}=$u+$\frac{1}{2}$\) at,
\(v_{1}=$\frac{v_{1}+c_{2}}{2}+$u+a t_{1}+$\frac{1}{2}$a t_{2}\)
\(v_{3}=$\frac{v_{2}+v_{2}}{2}=$u+a t_{1}+a t_{2}+$\frac{1}{2}$a t_{3}\)
So, \(\left($y_{1}-v_{2}\right)=-$\frac{1}{2}$a\left($t_{3}+t_{2}\right)\)
and \(\left($v_{2}-v_{3}\right)=-$\frac{1}{2}$\) a \(\left($t_{2}+t_{3}\right)\)
\(\therefore $\frac{\left(v_{1}-v_{2}\right)}{\left(v_{2}-v_{3}\right)}=\frac{\left(t_{1}+t_{2}\right)}{\left(t_{2}+t_{3}\right)}\)$

questions.q: A $2m$ wide truck is moving with a uniform speed ${v}_{0} = 8ms^{- 1}$ along a straight horizontal road. A pedestrian starts to cross the road with a uniform speed $v moving in a straight line,$when the truck is $4m$ away from him. The minimum value of $v$ so that he can cross the road safely is
questions.solution:
Let the man starts crossing the road at an angle θ shown in figure. For safe crossing the condition is that the man must cross the road by the time the truck describes the distance 4 + AC or 4 + 2 cot θ.


$∴ \dfrac{4 + 2 \text\cot \text{\theta}}{8} = \dfrac{2 / \text\sin \text{\theta}}{\text{v}}$

$\text{or} \text{v} = \dfrac{8}{\text{2} \text\sin \text{\theta} + \text\cos \text{\theta}} \text{...(1)}$

$\text{For minimum v,} \dfrac{\text{dv}}{\text{d} \text{\theta}} = 0$

$\text{or} \dfrac{- 8 \left(2 \text\cos \text{\theta} - \text\sin \text{\theta}\right)}{( \text{2} \text\sin \text{\theta} + \text\cos \text{\theta} {)}^{2}} = 0$

or 2 cos θ - sin θ = 0

or tan θ = 2



from Equation (1)

${v}_\min = \dfrac{8}{\text{2} ( \dfrac{2}{5} ) + \dfrac{1}{5}} = \dfrac{8}{5}ms^{- 1}$

questions.q:
Given below are the equations of motion of four particles A, B, C and D
${x}_{A} = 6t - 3; {x}_{B} = 4{t}^{2} - 2t + 3; {x}_{C} = 3{t}^{3} - 2{t}^{2} + t - 7;$ ${x}_{D} = 7cos ⁡ {60}^{o} - 3sin ⁡ {30}^{o}$

The particle moving with constant acceleration is
questions.solution:
${x}_{A} = 6t - 3$

${v}_{A} = \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(6t - 3\right) = 6$

Particle A moves with constant velocity.

${v}_{B} = \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(4{t}^{2} - 2t + 3\right) = 8t - 2, {a}_{B} = \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(8t - 2\right) = 8$

Particle B moves with constant acceleration

${v}_{C} = \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(3{t}^{3} - 2{t}^{2} + t - 7\right) = 9{t}^{2} - 4t + 1$

${a}_{C} = 18t - 4$

So, the particle moves with variable acceleration.

${x}_{D} = 7cos ⁡ {60}^{o} - 3sin ⁡ {30}^{o}$

Since ${x}_{D}$ does not depend upon time therefore particle is at rest.

questions.q: A body starts from rest and is uniformly accelerated for $30s$. The distance travelled in the first $10s$ is ${S}_{1}$, next $10s$ is ${S}_{2}$ and the last 10 s is ${S}_{3}$. Then ${S}_{1}: {S}_{2}: {S}_{3}$ is the same as
options: $1: 2: 4$
$1: 2: 5$
$1: 3: 5$
$1: 3: 9$
questions.solution:
a = constant

${S}_{1} = {v}_{0}t + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$

${v}_{1} = {v}_{0} + at$

${S}_{2} = {v}_{1}\text{t} + \dfrac{1}{2}{at}^{2}⇒ {v}_{0}t + \dfrac{3}{2}at^{2}$

${v}_{2} = {v}_{1} + \text{at}$

$= {v}_{0} + 2\text{at}$

${S}_{3} = {v}_{2}\text{t} + \dfrac{1}{2}{at}^{2}$

$= {v}_{0}\text{t} + \dfrac{5}{2}{at}^{2}$

${v}_{0} = 0$

${S}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}{at}^{2}$; ${S}_{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}{at}^{2}$; ${S}_{3} = \dfrac{5}{2}{at}^{2}$

${S}_{1}\text{:}{S}_{2}\text{:}{S}_{3} = \text{1}\text{:}3\text{:}5$

b^{2} & {d t^{2}}+$\frac{2}{b^{2}}\left(\begin{array}{l}$d y \\
d t

$\mathrm{(II)}\mathrm{Q}$ runs with speed $1 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ towards $\mathrm{P}$ while $\mathrm{P}$ remains stationary.
Note that irrespective of speed of $\mathrm{P}$, ball always leaves $\mathrm{P's}$ hand with speed $2 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ with respect to the ground. Ignore gravity. Balls will be received by $\mathrm{Q}$

one every $2 \mathrm{~s}$ in case $\mathrm{(I)}$ and one every $4 \mathrm{~s}$ in case $\mathrm{(II)}$
one every $3.3 \mathrm{~s}$ in case $\mathrm{(I)}$ and one every $2.5 \mathrm{~s}$ in case $\mathrm{(II)}$
one every $2.5 \mathrm{~s}$ in case $\mathrm{(I)}$ and one every $2.5 \mathrm{~s}$ in case $\mathrm{(II)}$

(I) Let initial distance between $\mathrm{P} \& \mathrm{Q}$ is $\mathrm{x}$
at $\mathrm{t}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{x}}{2}$ a receive the ball. Next ball. $\begin{array}{l} t_{2}=\frac{x-5}{2}+5 \\ \Delta t=\frac{5}{2} \end{array} (II) in second case at $t=0$\mathrm{P} throws the ball.
$t_{1}=$\frac{x}{3}. Next ball \begin{array}{l}$t_{2}=$\frac{x-5}{3}+$5 \\ $\Delta$t=$\frac{10}{3} \end{array}$

questions.q: A particle starts from rest and traverses a distance $2x$ with uniform acceleration, then moves uniformly over a further distance $4x$ and finally comes to rest after moving a further distance $6x$ under uniform retardation. Assuming entire motion to be rectilinear motion, the ratio of average speed over the journey to the maximum speed on its way is
questions.solution:
Let ${t}_{1}$,${t}_{2}$ and ${t}_{3}$ be the time taken by the particles to cover the distance $2x$, $4x$ and $6x$ respectively. Let $v$ be the velocity of the particle at $Bie$, maximum velocity. The particle moves with uniform acceleration from $A$ to $B$.

For motion from $A$ to $B$.

Average velocity $= \dfrac{0 + v}{2} = \dfrac{v}{2}$

Time taken, ${t}_{1} = \dfrac{2x}{\dfrac{v}{2}}$

Particle moves with uniform retardation from $C$ TO $D$, ${V}_{avg} = \dfrac{0 + v}{2} = \dfrac{v}{2}$

Time taken ,${t}_{3} = \dfrac{6x}{( \dfrac{v}{2} )}$

Total time $= {t}_{1} + {t}_{2} + {t}_{3}$

$t = \dfrac{2x}{v2} + \dfrac{4x}{v} + \dfrac{6x}{v2} = \dfrac{20x}{v}$

Average Velocity over $= \dfrac{6x + 2x + 4x}{\dfrac{20x}{v}} = \dfrac{3}{5}v$

Required Ratio $= \dfrac{Average Speed}{v} = \dfrac{3}{5}$
questions.source: Highly selective Backlog Qs for JEE Main

questions.q: The motion of a particle moving along the y-axis is represented as $y = 3\left(t - 2\right) + 5{\left(t - 2\right)}^{2}$. Identify the correct statement
options: the initial  \left(t = 0\right)$ velocity of the particle is $3\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$
the acceleration of the particle is $5\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$
the particle is at the origin at $t = 2s$
questions.solution:
We know that $\overset{\to}{v} = \dfrac{dy}{dt}$ & $\overset{\to}{a} = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{dv}}{dt}$
$v = \dfrac{dy}{dt} = 3 + 10 \left(t - 2\right)$
At $t = 0$ velocity $v = - 17ms^{- 1}$
$a = $\dfrac{dv}{dt} =$10ms^{- 2}$
$y = 3\left(t - 2\right) + 5{\left($t - 2\right)}^{2}$
At the value of $y$ will be $y = $3\left($2 - 2\right) + $5{\left($2 - 2\right)}^{2}$
therefore $y = 0$

questions.q: A particle starts from rest and has an acceleration of $2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ for $10 \mathrm\sec$. After that, it travels for $30 \mathrm\sec$ with constant speed and then undergoes a retardation of $4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ and comes back to rest. The total distance covered by the particle is
questions.solution:
Initial velocity $(u)=0$,
Acceleration \left(a_1\right)=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ and time during acceleration \left(t_1\right)=10 \mathrm\sec$.
Time during constant velocity \left(t_2\right)=30 \mathrm\sec$ and retardation \left(a_2\right)=-4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ (-ve sign due to retardation). Distance covered by the particle during acceleration, $\begin{gathered}$s_1=u t_1+$\frac{1}{2}$a_1 t_1^2=(0 $\times$10)+$\frac{1}{2} \times$2 $\times($10)^2 \\
=100 $\mathrm{~m}
\end{gathered}$And velocity of the particle at the end of acceleration, v=u+a_1 t_1=0+(2 $\times$10)=20 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s} .$Therefore distance covered by the particle during constant velocity \left(s_2\right)=v \times t_2$
=20 $\times$30=600 $\mathrm{~m}$Relation for the distance covered by the particle during retardation  \left(s_3\right)$ is $v^2=u^2+2 a_2 s_3$
or, $\quad(0)^2=(20)^2+2 \times(-4) \times s_3=400-8 s_3$
or, $s_3=400 / 8=50 \mathrm{~m}$
Therefore total distance covered by the particle s=s_1+s_2+s_3=100+600+50=750 $\mathrm{~m}$
